analysis: Market is in an uptrend (SPY +4.86% 20d slope), but our closed-trade record (PF 0.69, 5 consecutive stop-outs) demands selectivity. The lesson from recent losses: entries were made without clean basing confirmation or the stops were sized too tight relative to volatility. Today the book is 31% deployed with two healthy winners — A (+4.47%) and LII (+11.32%) — both thesis-intact; no action needed on either. With $69K cash and headroom for 1-2 more positions, I'm adding two high-quality businesses caught in Stage 1→2 basing setups at attractive valuations. AMP (Ameriprise) offers elite capital-light financials at a forward P/E of 9.5x with ROE near 67% — genuinely cheap for the quality. CDW is an IT distribution leader in confirmed uptrend basing at 36% of its 52w range, trading at fwd P/E ~11x with strong cash generation. Both carry earnings risk within 40 days, but as position-hold trades the thesis extends through earnings. No more than 2 new names given the recent loss streak — cash (~27%) remains a buffer. I will NOT force a third trade. The Sortino of -5.51 reflects the closed-trade losses; the open book is healthy. Primary risk-management discipline: tight ATR-based stops, proper sizing so worst-case per new name costs ~1-1.5% of equity.
